english.html: At last, the said de Rols being advised of the prodigious effrontery, horrible and strange imposture, which the said du Tilh had practised, substituting upon her the name and person of Martin Guerre her husband.

Because names are given or imposed only to distinguish and recognise persons, <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup> it is lawful for anyone, of his own free will, to take the name that seems good to him, and having taken it, to change it freely afterwards, provided that it is without fraud, and that the change is not to the detriment or damage of another <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>. For where the intention was bad, to defraud one's neighbour or to harm him in some way, it would then be a crime of forgery <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>, and thus punishable by death, civil death at the least <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. As for the substitution of persons, one cannot well give certain rules for it: for the ancients sometimes punished it, sometimes not; and when they punished it, sometimes sharply and with natural death, sometimes lightly, as we shall discourse below, God helping, in a more convenient place. <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup> Meanwhile, however, it will not be out of place to understand that in our law another kind of substitution is spoken of, namely when a wife substitutes in her husband's house a child as her own, which is nevertheless another's, to make it heir to the goods of her husband <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup> — a crime certainly grave, and surely repressed by the law, which was pleased to punish it not only in the person of the wife who had contrived and plotted the substitution, but also in all those who had given her counsel, favour and aid <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>; and although in other crimes some manner of impunity is gained by the passing of years <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>, nevertheless in this crime, he who is guilty does not escape the penalty by any lapse or interval of time whatsoever <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. ne de martin Guerre ſon mari.
Par ce que les noms ne ſont donnez ou impoſez que
pour diſcerner, & recongnoiſtre les perſonnes. {a} il eſt
loyſible, à vn chacun de gayeté de cœur, prendre le nom
qui luy ſemble, & l'ayant pris le changer librement a-
pres, pourueu que ce ſoit ſans fraude, & que le change-
ment ne ſoit au detriment, ou domage d'autruy {b}. car ou
l'intentiõ ſeroit mauuaiſe pour frauder ſon prochain, ou
luy nuire, en quelque ſorte: ce ſeroit lors vn crime de
faux {c}. & par ainſi puniſſable de mort pour le moins ci
uile {d}. Quand a la ſuppoſition des perſonnes, on n'en,
